 ATLANTA, GA – FEBRUARY 3: New England head coach Bill Belichick and owner Robert Kraft celebrate the Patriots’ 13-3 victory over the Los Angeles Rams in Super Bowl LIII at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia on February 3, 2019. (Staff Photo By Christopher Evans/MediaNews Group/Boston Herald) 
 By Andrew Callahan | acallahan@bostonherald.com PUBLISHED: November 8, 2026 at 3:26 PM EST | UPDATED: November 8, 2026 at 3:33 PM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Remember him?
 Bill Belichick returned to Foxboro late Saturday night to join the 2016 Patriots’ reunion party at Davio’s Steakhouse in Patriots Place, according to a report from MassLive. 
 Belichick drove north while his North Carolina team flew south following a 38-21 win at UConn, which kicked off at noon in East Hartford, Conn., roughly 30 minutes from Foxboro. Former Patriots players and coaches gathered at Davio’s hours after Rob Gronkowski was inducted as the newest member of the Patriots Hall of Fame in a ceremony outside Gillette Stadium.
 They also gathered on the eve of a planned 10-year anniversary celebration of their Super Bowl win over Atlanta scheduled to take place just before the Patriots play the Packers.
 Team owner Robert Kraft, who is recovering from back surgery, was not present Saturday, per MassLive, and told ESPN he will not attend Sunday’s game versus Green Bay on the advice of his doctors.
 Since his firing in Jan. 2024, Belichick has kept his distance from the organization, which he banned from sending scouts to North Carolina’s football practices last year. Tension between Belichick and Kraft has grown in recent years due to a variety of issues, including the owner’s public revelation that he had fired his head coach and the two had not mutually agreed to part ways, as they jointly announced in Belichick’s final press conference with the Patriots. Belichick’s last known appearance in Foxboro was in June 2024, when he attended Tom Brady’s Patriots Hall of Fame induction ceremony.
 It’s unclear if Belichick remained in the area following the Saturday dinner, or plans to be part of Sunday’s pregame celebrations with his former assistants and players, a group that includes Gronkowski, Julian Edelman, James White, Chris Hogan, David Andrews, Malcolm Butler, Patrick Chung and Stephen Gostkowski among others.
